name: Tupilak
description: The Tupilaq (tupilait pl.) is an Inuit (Greenland) avenging monster fabricated by an angakkuq (shaman) from animal parts (bone, skin, hair, sinew) and sometimes human remains, given life by ritual chants. Sent into the sea to destroy a specific enemy. Risky: if the target has greater magical power, the tupilaq rebounds to kill its maker—only public confession neutralizes it.
appearance: Inuit carved figure that contains spirit of ancestor or animal. Made from bone, skin, hair. Represent connection to ancestors and animals.
behavior: Inuit carved figure that contains spirit of ancestor or animal. Used as guardian, can protect or attack.
cultural_significance: Inuit spiritual objects. Represent connection to ancestors and animals. Used in shamanic practices.

name: Qalupalik
description: The Qalupalik (Qallupilluit) is an Inuit sea creature of Greenland and Arctic Canada that kidnaps children wandering too close to ice floes. Described as green-skinned, slimy, with long hair, webbed hands, scales, fins, wearing an amauti (woman's parka) made of eider feathers to carry victims. Emits a paralyzing shrill sound; snip can shape-shift (pilutitaminik).
appearance: Qalupalik is a humanoid from Greenland mythology.
behavior: Qalupalik is a humanoid from Greenland mythology. They are notorious for kidnapping children who wander too close to the shoreline, stuffing them into a large amauti (pouch) to take them to their underwater homes.
habitat: Cold Arctic waters, beneath ice floes, along shorelines near settlements. Lurks just below the surface, hidden from view. Most active during summer when children play near the water and during spring thaw when ice edges are unstable.
cultural_significance: Qalupalik is the most active cautionary figure in modern Greenland, still used by parents today to keep children safe from the very real danger of drowning in cold Arctic waters. It is the Greenlandic equivalent of the bogeyman, specifically adapted to the marine environment.
summary: A scaly sea-creature that kidnaps children who wander too close to the ice
fun_fact: The Qalupalik is a scaly aquatic creature of Inuit lore that kidnaps disobedient children from the shoreline.
seo_description: The Qalupalik is a scaly aquatic creature of Inuit lore that kidnaps disobedient children from the shoreline.
source: Boas, 'Qallupilluit' (InuitMyths.com); Christopher, 'The Qallupilluit Strange Beings from the Sea Depths'; Routledge, 'Do You See Ice?'; Inuit oral tradition (Nunavut, Greenland, Alaska)
